//: Server-side config store: API configs, connectors and the fetcher plan. Week 1 is structure only
//keys: A key starting with // is a comment; the loader skips it. A '//calls' block holds a fetcher's planned calls - inert until the prefix is dropped. 'env:NAME' is read from the environment at call time, never a committed secret. {{ ... }} tokens are substituted at call time. status: stub | planned | blocked | live.

llm_backends.//: Chatbot runs locally, so Ollama is the only AI backend. Reached over its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so llm_providers/openai_compatible.py serves it.
llm_backends.//migration: Currently built in config.py from OLLAMA_BASE_URL / OLLAMA_MODEL.

agents.//: Three agents, one backend, a separate system prompt each - routing, judging evidence and explaining someone else's output are different jobs. Prompts live with the agent code; only selection and sampling are config.
agents.job: Scope gating, request-type classification, input extraction, deciding what downstream work is needed.
agents.//detector_visibility: Reads only required_input_type and detector_configured. Never auth/request/response_mapping, never branches on mode; its output has no mode field.

agents.job: Judges scam_check from AddressContext when no detector is configured. Returns detection and explanation together, so the Forensic Investigator never runs here.
Explains a configured detector's evidence in plain language. Runs only when a detector is configured and is_llm_based is false.
agents.//faithfulness: Translation, not a second opinion. It must not re-judge, so a wrong value_map below becomes a confidently wrong explanation.

//active_detector: null = none configured, so scam_check falls through to the Scam Checker. That is what agents/business_analyser.py hardcodes today. Set to an id below to flip detector_configured true.

detectors.name: RektRadar
detectors.//timeout: Connector's job, not the mapping layer's. Timeouts and 4xx/5xx fail the same way, without running any mapping.
detectors.//auth: Free tier is anonymous and needs no key, which is how the evaluation ran. REKTRADAR_API_KEY is not in .env yet - a key is expected in Week 2, so the block is configured ready for it.

label.//: Score is numeric, not a word, so ranges derive the enum; first match wins. Fallback covers 40-69 and flags containing insufficient_data.

confidence.//: 0-100 to 0-1, clamped. Present-but-non-numeric is a MappingError, not a silent default.

evidence.//: Unknown code -> {description: raw code, weight: default_weight}.

honeypot.description: Token can be bought but not sold; funds get trapped.

sell_failed.description: Buys succeed but sells revert — classic honeypot.

lp_not_locked.description: Liquidity is neither burned nor locked, so it can be pulled.

unrestricted_mint.description: Supply can be minted with no access control.

no_renounce_ownership.description: The deployer still controls the contract.

previous_scam_tokens.description: The deployer has shipped previously flagged scam tokens.

response_mapping.//risk_type: Unmapped on purpose - RektRadar has no category field, so it stays null rather than guessed. Documented limitation.

detectors.//field_test: Free-tier evaluation: a fake or malformed address returns a normal low-risk result scoring 0 with NO error, so validate address format before calling or a fake address reads as safe. Score alone is not enough; read flags too. The API's own confidence field was 0 even on a clear scam, hence confidence is derived from score.

detectors.//no_mapping: Deliberately no request or response_mapping. The template's shared schema.py already emits DetectionResult, so the mapping layer never loads in template mode.
detectors.//endpoint: Loopback for dev. Config validation rejects non-https endpoints at save time, so the validator needs a localhost exemption or this will not save.
detectors.name: MyTemplateDetector

data_sources.//: Which API backs which fetcher. Endpoints and constraints only, no credentials.
data_sources.//traps: Two response shapes: account/contract/token return status+message, proxy is JSON-RPC and returns neither, so proxy success is result-vs-error presence. Applying the status check to proxy marks good responses as failed. HTTP 200 is not data: txlist with no transactions returns status '0' / 'No transactions found', a valid empty result; getsourcecode on an unverified contract still returns status '1' / 'OK' and the only tell is SourceCode == ''.
data_sources.//api_key: In .env. Missing key must fail immediately, not continue as None.

data_sources.//decision_needed: Intended liquidity source, no API key needed, but no project document records an endpoint path. Must be read off DexScreener's own docs before liquidity_fetcher can be written.
Open: Etherscan token search or a token list API such as CoinGecko. Best-effort by nature, so ambiguous matches are flagged, not guessed.

fetchers.//: Four context fetchers plus two resolvers. Each independently callable and independently failable, so one failure leaves the pipeline running on partial context. Each writes fetcher_provenance: which field it supplied and when.
fetchers.//invocation: Triggered conditionally by the Business Analyser, never all at once. scam_check: a resolver when raw input type does not match what is required, then context fetchers when required_input_type is address_with_context - always true on the Scam Checker path. address_info: only fetchers matching requested_fields.

//calls.//: verified_source = SourceCode != ''. Unverified returns SourceCode '' and the literal string 'Contract source code not verified' as the ABI.

Runtime, not constructor bytecode - creation bytecode is silently wrong for any contract with a constructor. is_contract is true only if code is neither 0x nor an EIP-7702 delegation (23 bytes, ef0100 + 20-byte address), which is still a wallet.

//calls.yields: hash, from, to, value, timestamp, method
//calls.//: 10,000 records per call max, so longer history needs page/offset. Zero-tx address returns status '0' / 'No transactions found' - not an error.

//calls.yields: tokenName, tokenSymbol, tokenDecimal, contractAddress - all the metadata tokens[] needs
//calls.//: No free way to list tokens held: tokeninfo is Pro, tokenbalance needs a known contract. Balance = sum incoming minus outgoing per contractAddress. That is an estimate and must be flagged as one.
Only once a specific token contract is known. Optional cross-check, not a primary call.

fetchers.//blocked: No documented endpoint, so the call shape cannot be written without inventing it. The Scam Checker's rug-pull and thin-liquidity checks read liquidity_usd and liquidity_events, and are on fake_data.py until this lands.

fetchers.//role: Resolves input, does not build context. Runs when raw_input.type is tx_hash but an address is required. Output is the address the context fetchers then run against.

//calls.//: JSON-RPC: numeric fields are hex, not the decimal strings txlist uses. Do not parse as decimal.
Only for contract-creation txs, where 'to' is null and the deployed address is the receipt's contractAddress.

fetchers.//blocked: See data_sources.token_name_source. A name matching several contracts stops the pipeline with a clarifying question; the mapping layer is never reached.

cache.//: Explorer APIs are rate limited, so results are held per address for a short TTL and follow-up turns reuse them. 5-10 min is the target; 600 is the top of it. Tune in Week 2.
